messages.subject: Moderated mediation binary dependent variable
parts:
Hi there,

I have a question about a moderated mediation model with a binary independent variable (X), a continous moderator (W), a continuous mediator (M) and a binary dependent variable (Y). I expect W to influence the X->M and X->Y paths. 
I would like to compute the index of moderated mediation described by Hayes with the lavaan package. 
I have built this code to try to estimate it:

Model1<-'
M<-a1*X + a2*W + a3*X:W
Y<-c1*X + c2*W + c3*X:W + b1*M
Index := a3*b1
'
Test<-sem(model =Model1, ordered="Y", data=Data_tot)

However, I systematically get this error message : 
Error in lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster, lavaan ERROR: some variables have no values (only missings) or no variance)

I have tried to run a simple mediation, it worked fine. I have tried this moderated mediation by treating Y as continuous, it worked fine as well. 

I understand that I could pass through Mplus or even the PROCESS macro since I have a simple level design but I do like lavaan and I would like to be able to compute this analysis with this package. Is there something wrong in my code or is this type of design unappropriate for lavaan yet? 

Thank you very much!

BF

parts: this package posits that a, b, and c paths are moderated, which is not my case here.
But you hypothesize that a and c are moderated.  Whether b is moderated is an empirical question (i.e., the M:W interaction could be estimated, and you predict it would not be significant, yes?).
I have to come back to Mplus?

I don't see why, but the error message is curious, especially because you don't get that message (right?) when you don't indicate Y is ordered.  Try fitting your model with the following option (not typically advisable), ONLY to be able to check for variables with all missing data or zero variance:

Test <- sem(model = Model1, ordered="Y", data=Data_tot, optim.force.converged = TRUE)
lavInspect(Test, "patterns") # check missing data patterns for variables with all NA
lavInspect(Test, "sampstat") # check for "variables" with zero variance on the diagonal

I don't see why

I have tried to fit the model on an entirely generated dataset and the error message was the same. Therefore, I thought that the problem was not in my data but was in the ability of lavaan to fit the requested model. Here are the generated data that leads to the same error message on my 2 computers (again, lavaan accepts to fit the model if Y is not declared as ordered). 

library(MASS)
set.seed(1234)
muX <- 4.9; sdX <- 1.7
muM <- 10.4; sdM <- 2.3
muW <- 7.0 ; sdW <- 1.6
sigmaTOT <- matrix(c(
sdX^2, sdX*sdM*0.4, sdX*sdW*0.4,
sdM*sdX*0.4, sdM^2, sdM*sdW*0.4,
sdW*sdX*0.4, sdM*sdW*0.4, sdW^2), 3)

Data_cont <- mvrnorm(246, mu = c(X=muX, M=muM, W=muW), Sigma = sigmaTOT)
Data_cat<-rbinom(246, 1, 0.44)
Data_tot2<-data.frame(Data_cont, Data_cat)

colnames(Data_tot2)<-c("X", "M", "W", "Y")
But you hypothesize that a and c are moderated.  Whether b is moderated is an empirical question (i.e., the M:W interaction could be estimated, and you predict it would not be significant, yes?).

Indeed, I think this is a possibility but (as far as I understand) the mediation package will assess the moderated mediation by performing: 
ind1 = a*b (for value W1 of the moderator) 
ind2 = a*b (for value W2 of the moderator) 
then compute the index of moderated mediation as ind1-ind2? 
Therefore, even if M:W on Y is low and not significant, as long as it is not equal to 0, it could increase my power to detect a significant moderated mediation compared to the classic way? (I am maybe missing something here)

Thanks again for your invaluable help!

messages.subject: Re: Moderated mediation binary dependent variable
parts:
Dear Terrence,

I think that I have found the problem. lavaan does not accept that the interaction term is only specified within the model when Y is declared as ordered. 
When the X:W term is created prior to the model construction (Data_tot$XW<-Data_tot$X*Data_tot$W), the following model works perfectly. 

Model1<-'
M~a1*X + a2*W + a3*XW
Y~c1*X + c2*W + c3*XW + b1*M 
Index := a1*b1
'
Test<-sem(model=Model1, data=Data_tot, ordered="Y")

I am not sure to understand why the X:W could be introduced directly in the model when Y is continuous but the main thing is that lavaan could be used for these data :)

Thanks again for your help, I would not have been able to detect that without your support. 

BF

messages.subject: Re: Moderated mediation binary dependent variable
parts: lavaan does not accept that the interaction term is only specified within the model when Y is declared as ordered.
I'm glad you tracked down the problem.
When the X:W term is created prior to the model construction (Data_tot$XW<-Data_tot$X*Data_tot$W), the following model works perfectly.

That's interesting.  I wonder if the "X:W" syntax would work if you simply set conditional.x = FALSE (and perhaps additionally fixed.x = FALSE).  It might have something to do with when the exogenous variables' effects are partialed out of the endogenous variables, versus when a product term is added to the analyzed covariance matrix.  By default, lavaan fits your model to residual polychorics to make estimation more efficient (I think that is consistent with Mplus, too).
